description: Model-selection benchmark. Header line first, then one LabeledTask per line. `correct_tier` is a human label; see README.md for the rubric, the evidence rules, and the known limitations.

title: test: fake-runner integration tests for orchestrator.run_once (heal & implement paths)
note: Merged on standard on the first attempt. One file, but designing a fake-runner harness for two orchestrator paths is real design work, not a mechanical edit.

title: skill: task-complexity-based model selection (learned)
note: Merged on light, but the 3-parallel retrospective recorded the verdict explicitly: 'the model-selection heuristic put haiku on non-trivial tickets'. A merge is not evidence the tier was right when the reviewer said otherwise.

title: feat: poll remote CI (gh checks) as an explicit pre-merge gate
note: PR #10 was correctly blocked on a failing unit test, then merged on the retry at the same tier. Standard was sufficient; the first attempt failed on care, not on capability.

title: chore: reference-set miner - extract one practice from a top-10 project's history
note: FAILURE MODE: the documented off-spec / code-free diff. Routed light on the 'chore:' prefix; the worker added a mypy step to CI instead of building the miner (PR #9, blocked), then timed out at 1200s on the retry. The merged commit contains a lesson note and no code. Two haiku attempts, zero delivered work.

title: feat: deepen the whitepaper synthesizer
note: Merged on standard, first attempt, one subsystem (knowledge.py + tests).

title: docs: add a one-iteration sequence diagram to ARCHITECTURE.md
note: OVER-PROVISIONED: ran on standard, but the merged change is a mermaid block in a single doc file. Nothing here needs a mid-tier model.

title: feat: reproduce-before-fix regression guard for heal and bugfix tickets
note: Merged on standard, first attempt, remote CI green - a new module plus wiring, but a single well-scoped mechanism. Ten touched files did not make it heavy.

title: feat: quota/cost telemetry ledger with a warn-then-halt per-block budget gate
note: New subsystem with a state machine (ok/soft/hard) threaded through orchestrator, cycle, governance, and config. Cross-cutting by construction.

title: chore: refresh reference-set snapshot and extract one practice
note: Merged on light, first attempt, remote CI green. Correctly routed: a data refresh plus one paragraph.

title: feat: worker trajectory store, JSON agent output, and `hsai replay`
note: New persistence layer, a CLI surface, and a change to how every agent run is invoked. size:L, and genuinely so.

title: feat: worker trajectory capture and working token/cost telemetry
note: Twenty-one files across config, ai, orchestrator, ledger, and the trajectory store. Correctly routed heavy.

title: governance layer - two-phase engine, SDLC evidence, review rhythm
note: The largest change in the repo's history: a new governance module, a CI gate, ADRs, and edits to eight existing modules.

title: fix: remote-CI-gated outcomes, CI parity guard, and ticket recovery
note: Three distinct reliability defects fixed together, each changing when the loop is allowed to merge. Correctness-critical and cross-module.

title: fix: make the loop safe for parallel workers
note: Only three files, but the change is a concurrency invariant (serialize the prologue, claim only unassigned tickets). File count is the wrong proxy here; getting it subtly wrong strands tickets.

title: refactor: keep MOC/whitepaper indexing out of parallel workers
note: Moving derived-index generation out of the worker path: one clear decision, three files, no new invariant.

title: feat: add per-agent timeout so a hung claude -p worker cannot stall the loop
note: A config key plumbed to a subprocess timeout. Ordinary feature work.

title: docs(knowledge): reindex MOCs after loop run
note: Regenerating derived index files. As mechanical as work in this repo gets.

title: feat: add a `--format` flag to `hsai status` and refresh the README table
body: Add a --format {text,json} option to hsai status. The JSON form must carry the same fields as the text form. Update the README's command table to document it.
note: FAILURE MODE (hand-authored, generalising ticket-004): light-signal words ('format', 'README') on a ticket whose acceptance criteria require new code and a new test. This is the shape that produced a code-free diff; a strategy that routes it light re-earns that incident.

title: chore: tidy up the lint configuration
body: Consolidate the ruff configuration and adopt the stricter rule set across src/ and tests/, fixing every violation it surfaces.
note: FAILURE MODE: the size:L override. Every keyword signal says light ('chore', 'lint'), but the planner sized it L. The label the planner set must win over words in the title.

title: feat: add a retry budget to the orchestrator
body: Cap total retries per block, not just per ticket. The gate must interact correctly with the existing attempts:N labels and the budget gate's soft/hard states.
note: A standard-shaped title carrying size:L. The override must hold even when nothing else about the ticket looks heavy.

title: docs: document the security model and the concurrency guarantees
body: Write a section in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describing the existing subscription-only guard and the single-writer-per-branch rule. No behaviour changes.
note: FAILURE MODE: a docs-shaped title that must not route heavy. 'security' and 'concurrency' are the subject matter, not the work. One doc file, nothing to reason about.

title: docs: rewrite ARCHITECTURE.md for the new orchestrator design
body: Bring the architecture document back in line with the code after the two-phase engine landed. Documentation only.
note: Same failure mode via 'architecture' and 'design'. Describing a design is not doing one.

title: fix: workers intermittently claim the same ticket under load
body: Two workers occasionally assign themselves the same issue when they start within the same second. Reproduce it first, then fix the claim path.
note: A real concurrency defect described in plain English - no 'race condition', no 'concurrency' in the text. Keyword lists cannot see this; 'intermittently' plus a heal kind should.

title: fix: typo in the README
note: The unambiguous light case. If a strategy misses this it is broken.

title: chore: bump ruff to 0.6.9
body: Update the dev dependency pin and fix anything the new release flags.
note: Mechanical dependency maintenance.

title: feat: add a `--since` filter to `hsai status`
body: Accept an ISO date and restrict the backlog snapshot to tickets touched since then. Needs argument parsing, a filter, and tests.
note: The unambiguous standard case: one subsystem, real code, no cross-cutting risk.

title: architecture: split the orchestrator into planner and executor stages
body: Separate deciding what to do from doing it, so the plan can be inspected and replayed before any side effect occurs.
note: The unambiguous heavy case.

title: security: scrub tokens from trajectory files before they are written
body: A trajectory captured a gh token in a tool result. Redaction must happen at the write choke point and must not be defeatable by a step that splits the secret across two fields.
note: Three files, but a secrets-leak fix that has to be right the first time. Security plus heal is the strongest pair of signals the harness has for 'do not economise here'.

title: refactor: rename `est_files` to `estimated_files` across the codebase
body: Pure rename. No behaviour change; the test suite must pass unmodified apart from the name.
note: FAILURE MODE: file count is not complexity. Nine files, zero judgement. The +3 bucket for 8-plus files pushes this the wrong way.

title: fix: flaky test in tests/test_orchestrator.py
body: The fake-runner test fails roughly one run in twenty. Find the ordering assumption and remove it.
note: Genuine debugging, but bounded to one test file. Standard is the right price.

title: docs: add a getting-started guide
body: A new page walking a reader from clone to first hsai run-once, plus a link from the README.
note: Prose only, two files. A single light keyword should not have to clear a -3 bar for this to route cheaply.

title: hard bug: race condition in the ledger append path
body: Concurrent workers interleave partial JSON lines. Reproduce under contention before fixing.
note: The unambiguous heavy case stated in the harness's own vocabulary.

title: chore: reference-set miner - extract one practice from a top-10 project's history
note: FAILURE MODE: ticket-004 as the router actually saw it. The orchestrator never estimates file counts, so every production decision is made with est_files at its default of 1 - which drops this ticket's score to exactly -3 and routes it light. ticket-004 records the same task with its measured file count; this row records the decision-time view. Keep both: the pair is the evidence that the file-count buckets are inert in production.

title: migration: move the knowledge base to the new frontmatter schema
body: Every existing note must be rewritten and the reader must accept both schemas during the transition.
note: A data migration with a compatibility window. Getting it wrong corrupts the knowledge base irreversibly.
